dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/5] Eligibility for study participation was based on a screening for self-reported depressive symptoms with the use of the Children's Depression Inventory (CDI). From an initial sample of 88 children, 23 children were selected to participate in the study on the basis of the following criteria: (1) a total CDI score of 8 or above and (2) parents consented and children assented to study participation. [/page/2/Text/6] On the basis of responses to the CDI items, algorithms were generated to match the DSM-IV criteria for major depression and dysthymic disorder. Using these algorithms, children were tentatively classified as meeting probable criteria for major depression (endorsed five-criterion depressive symptoms including depressed/irritable mood or anhedonia) and dysthymia/minor depression (endorsed three-criterion symptoms including depressed/irritable mood or anhedonia). Because the CDI assesses current state and does not include questions on duration of dysphoric mood, these algorithms should be viewed as identifying children who endorsed a sufficient number of core depressive symptoms as specified by DSM-IV but for whom the duration criteria was uncertain. Of the 23 children participating in the intervention phase of the project, 11 children (47.8%) met tentative criteria for major depression. Another 9 children (39%) met tentative criteria for minor depression/dysthymia (dysphoric mood plus two ancillary symptoms).
